title: Authenticated Server-Side Request Forgery in Dokploy via the AI provider `getModels` endpoint
summary:
## Summary

The `ai.getModels` tRPC query accepts a fully user-controlled `apiUrl` (`z.string().min(1)`, with no URL or host
validation) and performs a server-side `fetch(\${apiUrl}/models\)` from the Dokploy control-plane host, returning
content parsed from the response back to the caller. The endpoint is a `protectedProcedure` - reachable by **any
authenticated user, including a base-tier organization member** - and there is **no SSRF protection anywhere in the
codebase**. A low-privilege user can therefore make the server issue arbitrary outbound HTTP(S) GET requests to internal-only hosts, cloud metadata services, and other resources the attacker cannot reach directly, and read response content back.

This was confirmed live: a base-tier organization **member** queried `ai.getModels` with `apiUrl` pointing at an
internal-only service on the host's Docker network (not reachable from outside the host), and the Dokploy server
fetched it and returned the service's payload to the member.

## Severity

- **CVSS v3.1: 7.7 (High)** - `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`. An authenticated low-privilege user (base member)
  pivots the public API into the internal network the Dokploy control plane occupies. On typical VPS/cloud deployments
  this reaches link-local cloud-metadata (often instance/IAM credentials), internal databases, dashboards, and the
  Docker network, with response bodies read back - hence C:H and the scope change. Rises toward Critical wherever a
  metadata service exposing credentials is reachable.

## Vulnerable code

**Entry / auth - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/ai.ts:49-51`** (`protectedProcedure`, no `withPermission`, no org
check; `apiUrl` unvalidated):

```ts
getModels: protectedProcedure
  .input(z.object({ apiUrl: z.string().min(1), apiKey: z.string() }))
  .query(async ({ input }) => {
    const providerName = getProviderName(input.apiUrl);
    const headers = getProviderHeaders(input.apiUrl, input.apiKey);
    switch (providerName) {
      case "ollama": response = await fetch(`${input.apiUrl}/api/tags`, { headers }); break;   // attacker host
      case "gemini": response = await fetch(`${input.apiUrl}/models?key=...`, ...);     break;   // attacker host
      ...
      default:       response = await fetch(`${input.apiUrl}/models`, { headers });             // attacker host
    }
```

**Provider routing is pure substring matching on the attacker's own URL - `packages/server/src/utils/ai/select-ai-provider.ts:10-23`:**

```ts
export function getProviderName(apiUrl: string) {
  if (apiUrl.includes("api.openai.com")) return "openai";
  ... // a handful of fixed substrings
  return "custom";   // anything else -> getModels `default` branch -> fetch(`${apiUrl}/models`)
}
```

Any `apiUrl` that doesn't contain a known provider substring reaches `fetch(\${apiUrl}/models\)`; the `ollama`/
`gemini` branches also fetch the attacker-supplied host. Only `perplexity`/`zai`/`minimax` short-circuit to hard-coded
lists without a network call.

**Response read-back to the caller - `ai.ts:133-169`:**

- **Error path (full body):** `if (!response.ok) { const errorText = await response.text(); throw new Error(\Failed to
  fetch models: ${errorText}\); }` - the entire response body is returned verbatim in the tRPC error message.
- **Success path (structured):** `await response.json()` then the `id`/`name` fields of any array in the JSON (`res`,
  `res.models`, `res.data`, or the first array value of the object) are returned to the caller.

A repository-wide search for SSRF guards (`is_private`/`isPrivate`/`169.254`/`metadata`/`host-allowlist`/`validateUrl`)
shows none applied to these fetchers.
